name: AB Download Manager
description: Modern, lightning-fast open-source IDM replacement with browser integration.
axiom: Proprietary tools like IDM dominate Windows download acceleration through aggressive dynamic socket chunking but remain closed-source and platform-restricted. AB Download Manager re-engineers this multithreaded chunking architecture atop Kotlin and Jetpack Compose Desktop, delivering an open, transparent, and multiplatform IDM alternative.
highlights: Modern Jetpack Compose desktop interface
Native multi-part connection splitting and queue scheduling
Official Chrome and Firefox companion extensions
tradeoffs: Native BitTorrent protocol is not yet embedded; focused strictly on HTTP/HTTPS/FTP stream acceleration.

name: Gopeed
description: Ultra-high performance multi-protocol engine across all desktop and mobile platforms.
axiom: Aria2 established the gold standard for headless protocol multiplexing, but decoupling the CLI daemon from separate WebUI clients created significant operational friction. Gopeed unifies high-concurrency Go concurrency primitives with a reactive Flutter client into a single zero-dependency binary running identically across mobile and desktop.
highlights: Embedded BitTorrent, Magnet, and HTTP/FTP engine
Cross-platform mobile and desktop consistency
JavaScript extension ecosystem for custom extractors
tradeoffs: Does not bundle advanced stream scraping (HLS/DASH) natively without user-installed extensions.

name: Open Download Manager
description: Native Linux manager with unified queue for HTTP, Torrents, yt-dlp, and mirrors.
axiom: Linux desktop environments lack a cohesive, native download client that unifies diverse protocol engines. Open Download Manager solves this by orchestrating trusted system binaries (aria2, yt-dlp, and httrack) behind a native GTK4/Libadwaita interface with persistent crash-safe queue recovery.
highlights: Native GNOME/GTK4 look and feel
Unified queue across HTTP, Torrent, and video extractors
Tor and proxychains routing support
tradeoffs: Requires host dependencies (aria2, yt-dlp) or running via standalone AppImage.

name: Rayburst
description: High-throughput, modular download engine engineered for modern gigabit bandwidth.
axiom: Legacy download managers frequently bottleneck on high-bandwidth fiber connections due to memory allocation overhead and single-threaded queue arbitration. Rayburst leverages Rust zero-cost abstractions and asynchronous I/O to maximize bandwidth saturation with minimal CPU overhead.
highlights: Ultra-low memory footprint
High-concurrency async socket chunking
Modern clean architectural stack
tradeoffs: Relatively recent ecosystem; plugin support continues active development.

name: Mister Download Manager
description: Clean-room open-source download manager written in pure Rust with HTTP segmentation, torrents, and browser integration.
axiom: Traditional download accelerators either lock segmented HTTP engines behind proprietary licenses or depend on heavy garbage-collected runtimes. Mister Download Manager implements an RFC-compliant Rust download engine (mdm-engine) paired with BitTorrent (librqbit), yt-dlp, and cross-browser extensions in a single native workspace.
highlights: Clean-room Rust workspace with crash-safe resume and fuzz-tested engine crates
Native BitTorrent/magnet support alongside yt-dlp media and gallery-dl extraction
Companion extensions on Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons
tradeoffs: Young project; installers are not code-signed yet and macOS builds remain experimental.

name: Motrix
description: Full-featured, elegant desktop manager supporting HTTP, FTP, BitTorrent, and Magnet.
axiom: Complex torrent and multi-source download tooling historically suffered from cluttered, utilitarian interfaces. Motrix packaged the raw performance of aria2c within a polished, minimalist desktop interface that made advanced protocol downloading accessible to non-technical users.
highlights: Sleek, distraction-free user interface
Automatic tracker updating
Supports up to 64 concurrent download threads
tradeoffs: Electron runtime memory footprint is higher than pure native alternatives.

name: aria2
description: The definitive multi-protocol, multi-source command-line download accelerator.
axiom: Maximizing bandwidth utilization over unreliable networks requires simultaneous multi-source segment downloading across HTTP, FTP, and BitTorrent simultaneously. aria2 established the protocol-multiplexed chunking model that powers nearly all modern open-source download GUIs.
highlights: Negligible CPU and RAM overhead
Full JSON-RPC and XML-RPC remote control
Metalink and BitTorrent chunk verification
tradeoffs: Pure command-line tool; requires a separate WebUI or frontend client for desktop users.

name: Surge
description: Blazing fast Terminal User Interface (TUI) download manager built for power users.
axiom: Command-line downloaders like curl or aria2 lack dynamic, interactive terminal queue visualization without opening separate monitoring ports. Surge delivers an interactive keyboard-driven TUI that provides real-time chunk progress, speed graphs, and queue management inside SSH sessions.
highlights: Interactive terminal UI with keyboard shortcuts
Concurrent chunk acceleration in Go
Zero graphical dependencies
tradeoffs: Targeted specifically at terminal and server operators; no desktop browser extension.

name: Internet Download Manager (IDM)
description: Benchmark commercial download accelerator with robust browser catching.
axiom: Web browsers frequently drop long-running file transfers and throttle single-stream downloads. IDM implemented dynamic file segmentation with persistent socket reuse, establishing the de facto speed benchmark for Windows desktop download management.
highlights: Unmatched browser integration and dynamic video catching
Lightweight native Windows executable
Resilient resume capability
tradeoffs: Closed source, commercial license required after 30-day trial, Windows-only.

name: Free Download Manager (FDM)
description: Established all-in-one download manager supporting torrents and media.
axiom: Desktop users often juggle separate software for web downloads and BitTorrent transfers. FDM combines both into a single freeware client with scheduled traffic throttling and browser catching across all major desktop OSes.
highlights: Combined HTTP and BitTorrent queue
Traffic shaper to prevent bandwidth hogging
Native clients for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android
tradeoffs: Closed source freeware.

name: Prism
description: Cross-platform IDM-style manager with up to 32 connections per file, browser catching, video/MP3 via yt-dlp and torrents.
axiom: IDM's browser catching and segmented downloads are closed and Windows-only. Prism rebuilds that workflow as an MIT-licensed Rust engine (tokio, rustls) in a Tauri shell: it keeps every connection busy until the last byte and writes data to disk before it saves progress, so a crash or power loss resumes from the last byte it safely wrote.
highlights: Up to 32 connections per file, with per-host memory and polite back-off
Resume checks the file's size, ETag and Last-Modified so a changed file is never stitched from two versions
Browser extension for Chromium browsers and Firefox, video/MP3 through yt-dlp, BitTorrent and magnet links, queues and a scheduler
tradeoffs: Young project (first release in October 2026)
Installers are not code-signed and macOS builds are not notarized yet, so SmartScreen and Gatekeeper warn on first launch.

name: Xtreme Download Manager (XDM)
description: Veteran open-source download accelerator with streaming video grabbing, torrent support, and headless CLI mode.
axiom: Users migrating off proprietary accelerators need one tool that bridges multi-segment HTTP acceleration, HLS/DASH stream capture, and BitTorrent without switching apps. XDM separates its UI-agnostic download core (xdm-core) from a FlatLaf desktop shell and local browser-integration server.
highlights: Multi-connection segmented downloads with expired-link refresh
One-click HLS/DASH video grabbing via Chrome and Firefox extensions
Built-in torrent/magnet client plus headless CLI mode (xdm-app --headless)
tradeoffs: Version 9.x is undergoing an active rebuild in Kotlin/Java and relies on a JVM runtime.

name: Brisk
description: Modern cross-platform desktop download manager powered by a custom dynamic-reuse Dart engine.
axiom: Wrapping external CLI binaries like aria2 limits fine-grained socket scheduling and complicates packaging. Brisk implements a custom pure-Dart download engine from scratch that spawns connections dynamically and reassigns idle workers to remaining byte ranges until completion.
highlights: Custom Dart engine with dynamic connection spawn and byte-range reuse
M3U8 stream capture and multi-link extraction via companion browser extension
First-class packaging for Windows, macOS, Flatpak, Snap, and AUR
tradeoffs: Focused on HTTP and M3U8 streams without embedded BitTorrent support; Linux tarballs require keybinder-3 and appindicator3.

name: AriaNg Native
description: Standalone desktop client for AriaNg adding torrent file previews, tray controls, and magnet association.
axiom: Running AriaNg inside a regular web browser prevents OS-level protocol association, local file-system task creation, and background tray persistence. AriaNg Native packages the AriaNg UI inside Electron to bridge local OS integration with remote or local aria2 RPC daemons.
highlights: Drag-and-drop .torrent/.metalink preview with selective file downloading
Native magnet protocol handling, CLI arguments, and system tray minimization
Full parity with AriaNg multi-RPC host management
tradeoffs: Electron memory overhead; macOS Apple Silicon builds require clearing the quarantine attribute on first run.

name: Persepolis Download Manager
description: Lightweight Python/Qt GUI frontend for the aria2 download engine.
axiom: While aria2 provides unparalleled speed, non-developer users struggle with CLI flags and configuration files. Persepolis provides a native PyQt interface that manages aria2 daemon lifecycles transparently in the background.
highlights: Multi-segment downloading via aria2c
Video downloading integration
Scheduled queue downloads
tradeoffs: Relies on background daemon management which can occasionally desynchronize on non-standard OS setups.

name: uGet
description: Classic lightweight multi-connection download manager with clipboard monitoring.
axiom: Resource-constrained Linux installations need a download manager that uses minimal memory. uGet was written in pure C with GTK to provide multi-connection acceleration with virtually zero memory overhead.
highlights: Ultra-low memory footprint (< 30MB)
Dual backend engine support (curl or aria2)
Clipboard watcher and batch imports
tradeoffs: Infrequent maintenance cycles; older GTK3 interface.

name: Varia
description: GTK4/Libadwaita download manager uniting regular files, torrents, and video streams via aria2 and yt-dlp.
axiom: Modern GNOME desktops need an adaptive Libadwaita downloader that handles HTTP acceleration, BitTorrent, and media streams without exposing raw CLI flags. Varia coordinates aria2 and yt-dlp behind a native GTK4 UI distributed natively via Flathub, Snap, and desktop installers.
highlights: Native GTK4/Libadwaita design with official Flathub and Snap packages
Unified queue for HTTP files, torrents/magnets, and yt-dlp video/audio
Companion Firefox and Chrome integrator extensions
tradeoffs: Depends on underlying aria2 and yt-dlp backends; macOS Intel builds update less frequently than Apple Silicon.

name: DownThemAll!
description: Advanced in-browser batch download utility with regex filtering.
axiom: Downloading dozens of links or images from a webpage manually is tedious and prone to rate limits. DownThemAll! introduces advanced batch pattern matching and multi-stream acceleration directly inside browser tabs without external executables.
highlights: 1-click download of all page media
Regular expression filename mask filters
Zero external binary dependencies
tradeoffs: Subject to browser WebExtension API limitations on socket management.

name: Chrono Download Manager
description: Complete download manager integrated directly inside the browser tab.
axiom: Traditional browser download shelves are minimal and lack queue management. Chrono replaces the default Chromium downloads shelf with a full tab-based management console, video sniffer, and batch downloader.
highlights: Replaces default browser download shelf
Built-in media sniffer for video and audio
Customizable rule filters
tradeoffs: Closed source.

name: Motrix WebExtension
description: Browser extension that automatically forwards browser downloads to Motrix and compatible aria2 forks.
axiom: Desktop aria2 GUIs like Motrix cannot intercept browser click-to-download flows without a bridge inside the browser's downloads API. Motrix WebExtension captures download events and dispatches them over authenticated JSON-RPC with configurable port and secret keys.
highlights: Automatic browser download interception with RPC secret authentication
Published on both Chrome Web Store and Mozilla Add-ons (Edge/Opera compatible)
Automated Playwright end-to-end test suite
tradeoffs: Requires Motrix to already be running in the background; cannot auto-launch the desktop client.

name: Aria2 Explorer
description: Chromium extension integrating AriaNg monitoring, smart download capture, and multi-server aria2 RPC routing.
axiom: Power users running local or remote aria2 daemons need both automated download capture and a full task-management console inside the browser. Aria2 Explorer embeds AriaNg directly in popup, tab, window, and side-panel views with URL pattern routing and cookie/header forwarding.
highlights: Rule-based auto capture by size, extension, and domain with Alt-key bypass
Embedded AriaNg WebUI supporting popup, tab, window, and side-panel modes
Multi-RPC server switching with URL pattern matching and cookie forwarding
tradeoffs: Chromium-only (Chrome/Edge); requires an external aria2 daemon with RPC enabled.

name: AriaNg
description: Modern, zero-runtime web frontend for managing headless and self-hosted aria2 daemons.
axiom: Headless aria2 servers on NAS boxes and homelabs expose only JSON-RPC/XML-RPC endpoints without an administrative interface. AriaNg delivers a complete, responsive management console in pure static HTML and JavaScript that requires no server-side compiler or runtime.
highlights: Zero server-side runtime; deployable as static files or single-file All-In-One HTML
Responsive desktop and mobile layout with incremental RPC polling
Multi-RPC host support, task sorting/filtering, speed charts, and BitTorrent peer inspection
tradeoffs: Frontend UI only; requires an existing aria2 daemon and standard builds must be served over HTTP rather than file://.

name: pyLoad
description: Pure Python lightweight download manager designed for NAS, Homelabs, and servers.
axiom: Servers, NAS appliances, and Docker homelabs require an always-on headless download service that can be managed via Web UI, mobile app, or CLI without running a desktop environment. pyLoad provides a modular server architecture with built-in CAPTCHA handling and hoster plugins.
highlights: Headless core with responsive Web UI
Extensive plugin system for file hosters
REST API for remote automation
tradeoffs: Requires container or Python environment setup.
